idea: Listed property and REIT research with an architect's eye
buyer: Real estate and generalist PMs holding listed property
pain: Property analysts model cash flows without judging the assets themselves
v1: One REIT initiation assessing scheme quality alongside the numbers
verdict: The clearest expression of her rare combination, sold to a buyer she can already reach.

why.distribution: 20-50 warm PMs, and real estate desks are a defined, findable segment within them.
why.demand: Property research is a paid category; her specific angle is untested.
why.fmf: Requires both halves - institutional analysis and genuine architectural judgement. Almost nobody else has both.
why.revenue_structure: Annual research subscription that embeds into a desk's process.
why.defensibility: The combination is the moat, and a back catalogue of assessed assets compounds.
why.capital: Property data and site visits: under £2k to start.
why.time_to_revenue: A pilot subscriber from her network in 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: Real but slow; listed property is out of favour, offsetting the retrofit and repricing story.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,200/mo x 15 funds = £216k gross less ~£12k data = £204k net, on annual upfront contracts. Fifteen real estate desks is a defined universe she can name. Monthly billing drops year one to ~£115k.
carries: The one idea where her two careers are both load-bearing, sold at institutional prices to a warm buyer.
kills: Nothing structural. The risk is that PMs treat asset quality as unquantifiable and refuse to pay for judgement.
test: Send two real estate PMs a free assessment of a REIT they hold, then quote £1,200/mo.
test_pass: One says it changed their view, or asks about a contract.
test_fail: They say it is interesting but not investable.
